title: London City Lionesses fall 2-1 to Manchester City
content:

title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or celebration turns into anxiety‑filled hangover for Bayern Munich
content:
Bayern Munich’s celebration of Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or victory took a somber turn during their recent match against Borussia Dortmund. Prior to the game, the club held a guard of honor for the England captain, who had been awarded the prize two nights earlier. The pre-match atmosphere was festive, with Kane appearing on the stadium’s giant scoreboard holding the golden trophy and smiling, marking a significant milestone in his partnership with the club.

However, the anticipated victory lap did not materialize. Dortmund did not follow the expected script, resulting in a draw that left the defending champions level on points with the visitors at the top of the table. The outcome shifted the mood from the celebratory pre-game ceremony to a more anxious reality for Bayern Munich, as the competitive nature of the classic fixture ultimately overshadowed the individual accolade.
summary: Harry Kane's Ballon d’Or trophy was celebrated by Bayern Munich players, who welcomed him onto the pitch with a guard of honour. The party, however, turned into an anxiety‑filled hangover for the club.

title: Bucs win 16-0 vs Falcons with zero passing yards
content:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers completed a 16‑0 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, a game in which the team recorded zero passing yards.  The Bucs attempted only three passes, all of which were incomplete, and Baker Mayfield was the only quarterback involved in the passing attack.

Mayfield’s three attempts marked the first time a Buccaneers team has gone a game without a single completed pass since the Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 16‑12 on 29 September 1974.  The game was played in a heavy downpour that prompted the Bucs to rely almost exclusively on their ground attack.

The rushing effort was the centerpiece of the win.  Tampa Bay carried the ball 56 times for 324 yards, the most rushing yards ever achieved by the franchise in a single game.  Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown, while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards on the ground.

In the rain‑slick conditions, Mayfield’s role was largely limited to blocking for the running backs, and the Buccaneers’ success hinged on their dominant rushing performance.
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated the Atlanta Falcons 16-0, completing zero passes in the game. Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown while Kenneth Gainwell added 140 yards, and the team amassed 324 rushing yards on 56 carries, the most in a single game in franchise history.

title: England’s early exit from Rugby League World Cup highlights need for systemic change
content:

Damning remarks about the state of English rugby league were first made by former Kangaroos coach Ricky Stuart almost two decades ago. Stuart delivered the comments after England’s men were beaten in the semi‑finals of the 2008 Rugby League World Cup, and his stance remains influential today.

England has failed to reach the last four for the first time, having not qualified from an arguably farcical group‑stage format. The result underscores the urgency of the reforms called for by the sport’s critics.
summary: Former Australia coach Ricky Stuart criticised England’s rugby league after the 2008 semi‑final loss, and his remarks still carry weight. England’s early exit from the Rugby League World Cup, the first time they failed to reach the last four, underscores a need for systemic change and a higher priority for the national side.

title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 world champion at 20
content:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli made history this year by becoming Formula One’s youngest world champion at 20 years old, a record that also marked Italy’s first championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The story began before the 2026 season, when most of the F1 community believed Mercedes had the fastest car and George Russell was the favourite for the title. Antonelli, then a teenage teammate, was seen as a prodigious talent who would need further development after a challenging rookie season.

That consensus lasted only one race. By the sixth round, Antonelli had turned expectations on their head, establishing himself as a serious contender for the championship. Observers noted his strong performance in a car that dominated the first two‑thirds of the season, and praised his verve, aggressive skill, judgment, and moments of maturity that belied his age.

Antonelli’s triumph is notable not only for the record it set but for the manner in which he achieved it, drawing attention to his rapid growth and competitive spirit on the track.
summary: Kimi Antonelli, a 20‑year‑old Mercedes driver, won the Formula One World Championship in his second season. He became the youngest champion and Italy's first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

title: Europe could face colder weather as polar vortex weakens
content:
Disruption to winds above the Arctic threatens to alter weather patterns across parts of Europe in the coming weeks. The stratospheric polar vortex over the northern hemisphere is facing an unusually early weakening, a shift that normally would not occur until later in the season.

Forecast models indicate the vortex could weaken significantly over the next ten days, when it would typically be strengthening. A major sudden stratospheric warming (SSW) event is possible, which could influence weather patterns in the following weeks by increasing the likelihood of persistent areas of high pressure across the mid‑latitudes and colder conditions weeks later.

title: MIT researchers use super‑flexible ligands to create customizable nanoparticle materials
content:
Researchers from MIT and the University of Delaware have developed a new method for assembling nanoparticles into designer materials, published in Nature Materials. The approach utilizes super-flexible connector molecules, or ligands, that intentionally deform based on their surrounding environment to regulate the packing of nanoparticle networks. By leveraging connector flexibility and electric charges, the team demonstrated how to tune the structure of these networks, creating new kinds of nanoparticle-based materials. This technique aims to overcome previous limitations in controlling the number and direction of links between particles, offering a more versatile pathway for applications in photonics, chemical catalysis, medicine, and agriculture.

Traditional methods for creating nanoparticle superlattices often relied on changing particle shapes or aligning rigid connector chains. However, these approaches limited the possible material structures and were difficult to scale because they required specific, bespoke synthesis methods that worked only under certain conditions. Rob Macfarlane, the Richard P. Simmons (1953) Professor in Metallurgy in MIT’s Department of Materials Science and Engineering, noted that the prevailing dogma for 20 years was that connector ligands needed to be rigid to prevent assembly failure. The new research challenges this view by demonstrating that extreme flexibility can be just as effective, allowing ligands to reorganize as particles come together.

In the new system, the nanoparticles feature flexible ligands with electrically charged tips, where positive and negative charges attract one another. This allows the bonds to be as flexible as desired, spontaneously moving toward configurations that maximize bond stability. Experiments led by MIT PhD candidate Nicholas Sbalbi showed that researchers could control the connections by altering nanoparticle sizes and ligand chain lengths. The amount of polymer flexibility dictates the number of bonds each particle forms, enabling the creation of lattices with fewer bonds per particle than previously possible using rigid connectors.

The team successfully assembled the nanoparticles into previously unseen crystal structures without needing to predesign specific connection points or particle shapes. Macfarlane explained that this method allows for less dense formations of nanoparticles, which opens up interesting applications that are limited by traditional dense packing. The researchers believe this establishes ligand flexibility as a new path for customizing material structures at scale, moving toward independent control over both the particle properties and the resulting assembly.

In addition to Macfarlane and Sbalbi, the paper includes contributions from University of Delaware doctoral student Stephen Kronenberger, MIT undergraduate Hana Shinzawa, Matthew Ye PhD ’26, and former University of Delaware professor Arthi Jayaraman. The research was supported in part by the National Science Foundation, the Department of Energy, the U.S. Army, and the U.S. Navy.
summary: Creating better-performing materials comes down to having more control over their structure at the smallest possible scale. One particularly effective way to accomplish that is using nanoparticles, which have highly customizable shapes and sizes and have already shown promise in applications across energy, medicine, and electronics.

summary: Scientists uncovered DNA evidence that Europeans living more than 30,000 years ago were connected across vast distances. Genetic clues from human remains and cave sediments reveal prehistoric migration, long‑lasting communities and survival during the harshest Ice Age conditions.

title: Review finds little reliable evidence that medical cannabis improves sleep
content: A major new review questions the growing enthusiasm for medical cannabis as a treatment for insomnia, reporting little reliable evidence that it improves sleep quality, sleep duration or daytime functioning. Researchers note that the lack of evidence reflects weak existing studies rather than proving cannabis ineffective.
summary: A major new review found little reliable evidence that medical cannabis improves sleep quality, sleep duration, or daytime functioning. Researchers said the findings do not prove cannabis is ineffective, but indicate that existing studies are too weak to determine its effectiveness.
author: Science Daily

title: Moderate drinking linked to cancer and early death, major study finds
content: A major new study finds that even modest alcohol consumption raises the risk of cancer, heart disease and premature death. The researchers reported no overall health benefits from drinking and cautioned that intake exceeding one alcoholic beverage per day can markedly increase long‑term health risks.
summary: A major new study found that even relatively small amounts of alcohol increase the risk of cancer, heart disease, and premature death. Researchers reported no overall health benefits from drinking and warned that consuming more than one alcoholic beverage per day can significantly raise long‑term health risks.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA's Hubble and Webb find 27 unchanged distant objects beyond Neptune
content: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes examined 27 small objects located beyond Neptune, uncovering clues about the solar system’s origins. Researchers found these distant bodies are ancient planetary building blocks that have stayed largely unchanged for billions of years, and their surprising sizes and abundances pose challenges to current models of planet formation.
summary: NASA’s Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes studied 27 tiny, distant objects beyond Neptune to investigate the solar system’s origins. Scientists found the ancient building blocks have remained remarkably unchanged for billions of years, and their unexpected sizes and numbers challenge existing theories of planet formation.
author: Science Daily

title: IceCube detects ghost particles with energy 10 billion times solar neutrinos
content: IceCube has detected neutrinos—often called “ghost particles”—with energies about ten billion times greater than those produced by the Sun. Using its massive detector embedded in Antarctic ice, scientists observed these extremely energetic particles arriving from distant cosmic sources. Researchers note that such neutrinos may provide clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events and other fundamental mysteries.
summary: IceCube, a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice, has detected neutrinos—called ghost particles—with energy about 10 billion times that of solar neutrinos. The particles arrive from distant cosmic sources and could provide clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and other universal mysteries.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Perseverance rover sets record by traveling 28.10 miles on Mars
content: NASA’s Perseverance rover has traveled 28.10 miles on Mars, establishing a record for the greatest distance covered by any vehicle on another world. The rover’s achievement is credited to its autonomous navigation system and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, which continue to expand the limits of robotic exploration.
summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover has traveled 28.10 miles on Mars, setting a historic record as the farthest distance driven by any vehicle on another world. The rover uses autonomous navigation technology and advanced driving capabilities to push the boundaries of robotic exploration.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA satellites capture skull-shaped ice formation on remote Antarctic island
content: NASA satellites have photographed a skull‑shaped formation on a remote Antarctic island. The feature’s eerie outline is linked to unusually warm winter temperatures that have exposed extensive dark ice, a condition scientists say could speed future glacier melt and gradually alter the formation’s appearance.
summary: NASA satellites captured an eerie skull-shaped formation on a remote Antarctic island. Unusually warm winter temperatures have exposed dark ice, potentially accelerating melting and gradually changing the formation’s appearance.
author: Science Daily

title: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines overlook potassium's role
content: Scientists say current high‑blood‑pressure guidelines overlook a key factor, arguing that increasing potassium intake may be as important as lowering salt. A new report finds that pairing higher potassium consumption with reduced sodium could provide greater blood‑pressure control than sodium reduction alone, prompting calls for a major rethink of management strategies.
summary: Scientists say current high blood pressure guidelines need a major rethink because eating more potassium could be as important as cutting back on salt. A new report finds that combining increased potassium intake with reduced sodium consumption may offer greater benefits for blood pressure control than sodium reduction alone.
author: Science Daily

title: Student astronomy guide at Sydney Observatory reshapes talks after child’s question
content:
A first‑year science student secured a position as an astronomy guide at Sydney Observatory, where she led groups of about 20 visitors. When clear, the tours involved viewing stars and planets through the observatory’s telescopes; when cloud cover obscured the sky, the experience shifted to a 3D theatre and the on‑site planetarium to explore the wider universe.

In the planetarium her preferred feature to present was the Hubble Ultra Deep Field image. She described how the Hubble Space Telescope observed a tiny patch of sky—roughly the size of a grain of sand held at arm’s length—for eleven days, gathering enough light to reveal distant galaxies. The reveal often prompted an audible gasp from at least one audience member.

An eight‑year‑old’s question about black holes later caused her to reconsider the examples she used, prompting a reassessment of how to explain the concept in a family‑friendly way.
summary: Student astronomy guide at Sydney Observatory reshapes talks after child’s question.
author: Guardian Science

title: ESMO trial tests mRNA vaccine plus pembrolizumab in 1,137 high‑risk melanoma patients
content: Many treatments are now extending lives, but the measure of progress should not end with a scan or a survival curve Two decades ago, a dear friend called me in a trembling voice. Was there hope for his young nephew, whose cancer had spread to the brain? Sadly, “no”, I said. But today, for such patients, there are options that were unimaginable back then. Recently, researchers at the European Society For Medical Oncology presented the latest chapter results from a randomised controlled trial of a bespoke cancer vaccine for patients with high-risk melanoma. The trial involved 1,137 patients whose melanoma had been surgically removed but remained at high recurrence risk. They received either pembrolizumab, an established immunotherapy, or pembrolizumab combined with an experimental mRNA vaccine, designed to help the immune system recognise and attack targets unique to the patient’s tumour.
summary: Researchers at the European Society For Medical Oncology presented results from a randomised controlled trial of a bespoke cancer vaccine for high‑risk melanoma. The trial enrolled 1,137 patients whose melanoma had been surgically removed and compared pembrolizumab alone with pembrolizumab combined with an experimental mRNA vaccine.

title: NASA Landsat images fall colors in Pennsylvania’s “Grand Canyon”
content: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Pennsylvania’s Grand Canyon Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 25, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison North-central Pennsylvania is canyon country with an Appalachian flair. Pine Creek Gorge reaches depths of about 1,500 feet (460 meters) along its gently curving path through the forests of the Allegheny Plateau. Instead of the steep rock walls characteristic of canyons in the desert Southwest, lushly vegetated slopes outline the dramatic topography. In autumn, greens give way to a palette of reds and golds sought out by leaf peepers. Nicknamed the “Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania,” the gorge runs for some 45 miles (72 kilometers) from Ansonia south to Pine Creek’s confluence with the West Branch Susquehanna River, reaching its greatest depths around Waterville. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite captured this image of Pine Creek Gorge on October 25, 2026, when colorful fall foliage was on display. Glaciers played a key role in the canyon’s formation, though ice itself did not carve it. Pine Creek once flowed to the north, opposite of what it does today. As glaciers advanced into the region from the northeast during the last ice age, they dammed the river and filled the valley with lakes. Those lakes eventually overflowed, sending water streaming to the south. Autumn colors emerge along Pine Creek Gorge in this view from Colton Point State Park on October 11, 2009. Fishhawk, via Flickr When the ice receded, Pine Creek was already becoming entrenched in its southward course. Rocks and sand left behind by the melting ice further prevented the water from turning back north. Glacial meltwater continued to rush through the valley, deepening and shaping it into its current form. Today, the hillsides around the gorge are blanketed in northern hardwood and mixed oak forest, sprinkled with hemlock and white pine. In autumn, the deciduous trees impart red and gold hues to the landscape akin to the rock of the famous Arizona canyon. October 9 October 25 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 9 October 25 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 9 October 25 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Image Details Foliage in the northern hardwood and oak forests around Pennsylvania’s Pine Creek Gorge takes on fall color between October 9, 2026 (left), and October 25, 2026 (right). The images were acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8. NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison. This seasonal change around Pine Creek Gorge has not always been so visually pleasing. With increasing demand for wood products in early 19th-century America, loggers found their way to the area’s stately trees. At the time, white pine and hemlock several feet in diameter and towering hardwoods populated the slopes around Pine Creek Gorge. The pines were especially valued for making ship masts, and hemlock bark was used to tan leather. Before railroads, logs were floated down Pine Creek to the Susquehanna in massive drives. By the early 20th century, decades of logging left the land so barren that the area earned the moniker “Pennsylvania Desert.” The forest has since returned, and with it, wild inhabitants such as black bears, coyotes, bobcats, timber rattlesnakes, and a diversity of songbirds. In 1968, an area of 30,000 acres (12,000 hectares) was designated a National Natural Landmark. Visitors can experience the gorge’s natural splendor at many points along its path, including from multiple state parks and the Pine Creek Rail Trail. A Long Cloud on Mars Explanation: What’s causing this unusually long cloud on Mars? Known as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and first recorded by NASA’s Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977, the strange cloud has been imaged in greater detail more recently by ESA ’s robotic Mars Express spacecraft. The featured image is from 2018. The cloud forms only during spring and summer seasons and then only during morning hours. Made of water-ice, the most familiar process that causes cloud crystals to form around bits of dust would fail due to the thinness and lack of dust high in the Martian atmosphere. Leading speculation holds that dust is not involved. After the cloud forms near the volcano Arsia Mons, wind blows the cloud downstream — creating a tail that can extend over 1500 kilometers. Efforts to better understand AMEC s will continue, an understanding that may bolster a more complete view of cloud formation on Earth. title: Agentic web emerges as AI agents transform internet; cities pursue safer roads
content:
The weekday newsletter The Download offers a snapshot of two contrasting technology‑driven trends. In its opening segment, the publication notes that the “agentic web” is moving from concept to practice. Tim Berners‑Lee first outlined a vision in 2001 for an internet run by autonomous software agents that would handle tasks without users needing to navigate browsers or search engines. The newsletter says that, a quarter‑century later, AI agents are beginning to fulfill that vision: they can triage email inboxes, perform grocery shopping and even access bank accounts. The piece labels this emerging layer of the internet the “agentic web” and observes that it will transform the online experience, while leaving open the question of whether the “human web” will survive the shift.

The second feature turns to road safety, highlighting the scale of traffic‑related fatalities. According to the newsletter, more than 1 million people die in traffic crashes each year, making these incidents the leading cause of death for children and young adults worldwide. It points out that inexpensive, proven measures—such as tightening intersections with planters and lowering speed limits—can improve safety, but that governmental red tape often slows implementation. Nevertheless, the article cites examples of cities that are making progress by investing in public transit, extending curbs and deploying cameras to identify dangerous zones that need redesign.

Both sections are presented as part of broader editorial projects. The agentic web story appears under the byline of Grace Huckins, while the traffic‑death analysis is authored by Sara Kiley Watson and is identified as the final installment of the “Are we there yet?” series, which evaluates six long‑promised technologies on a progress meter. The newsletter invites readers to subscribe for the remaining five installments in the series.

Beyond these two topics, The Download lists a series of other technology headlines, ranging from market moves in AI and crypto to cybersecurity incidents and emerging scientific developments. Each item is accompanied by a brief description and a source citation, but the newsletter does not elaborate further within this edition.
summary: AI agents are beginning to make the agentic web a reality, handling tasks such as inbox triage, grocery shopping, and bank account access. Some cities are reducing traffic deaths by investing in public transit, extending curbs, and using cameras to spot dangerous road zones.

title: HPE hybrid AI platform cuts token costs 30‑50% by measuring cost per merged pull request
content:
A developer‑focused AI agent does far more than answer a single prompt. It plans, writes code, runs tests and iterates, often consuming ten to fifty times more tokens than a basic chat interaction. Because many pricing models charge per token, the most valuable workflows can also become the most costly. Recent examples include Uber, which reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot’s shift from flat‑rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner forecasts that AI‑coding token costs will exceed average developer salaries by 2028.

The article argues that token counts are an imperfect metric for value, proposing cost per merged pull request as a more meaningful measure. This metric divides total AI‑assisted development cost by the number of changes that pass review and are merged, while also tracking rework and defects to ensure quality is not sacrificed. If the cost per merged pull request falls as AI usage rises, developers are converting higher consumption into useful software.

A suggested approach is to match the model to the task. High‑cost, frontier models or on‑premises flagship models can be reserved for complex planning and novel reasoning, while routine work such as code generation, test creation and refactoring can be routed to open‑weight models operated internally. A gateway can direct requests based on task complexity, data sensitivity, cost and latency, allowing premium inference to be applied only when justified.

Ownership of inference capacity changes the economics. With rented inference, each call adds to the bill; with owned capacity, most costs are fixed upfront, making additional calls cheaper as usage grows. Owned capacity also keeps proprietary code inside the enterprise, limiting external exposure to only approved planning prompts. HPE’s hybrid AI platform, which routes routine workloads from more than 150 internal applications to on‑premises open‑weight models, reportedly reduced token costs by 30‑50 percent. The company tracks cost per active developer and cost per merged pull request to assess the impact of moving to owned capacity.

The piece concludes that most enterprises will adopt a hybrid model—using frontier APIs for demanding or intermittent tasks and owned capacity for repeatable volume—governed by a gateway that protects code sovereignty. As AI‑assisted development expands, the choice lies between higher variable‑cost bills and greater software output on owned infrastructure. Companies that succeed will build operating models where increased AI use improves economics rather than merely inflating costs.
summary: HPE’s hybrid AI platform routes routine coding workloads to open-weight models on premises, reducing token costs by 30‑50%. It tracks cost per active developer and cost per merged pull request to link AI spending to software shipped, recommending a hybrid mix of frontier APIs and owned capacity.

title: WIRED finds 400 Chinese-language AI apps with hidden violent deepfake features
content: WIRED reported that roughly 400 Chinese‑language apps and websites marketed as ordinary AI tools contain concealed functions that enable users to produce sexually abusive deepfake content and violent AI‑generated images and video. The investigation found these hidden features were embedded in the platforms despite their seemingly mundane appearance.
summary: WIRED uncovered about 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that appear to be ordinary AI tools. The apps contain secret functions that let users create violent AI‑generated images and video.
author: Wired

title: Writer receives nearly 2,000 misdirected political fundraising texts
content: An individual reports receiving nearly 2,000 campaign‑fundraising text messages that were intended for another recipient. In probing the cause, the person says the inquiry exposed a complex network of politicians, data brokers and questionable tactics behind the misdirected spam.
summary: The author got almost 2,000 campaign fundraising texts that were meant for someone else. Their inquiry uncovered a labyrinth of politicians, data brokers, and shady tactics.
author: Wired

title: Guidance on When to Use AI Chatbots vs Traditional Search Engines
content: Chatbots can often retrieve the information you want from the web effectively. However, the content notes that there are occasions when typing a query into a traditional search engine will produce better results.
summary: Chatbots are often quite good at retrieving the information you want from the web. However, sometimes you’ll get better results by typing your query into a good old search engine.
author: Wired

title: European supermarkets report freezer hacks raising temperatures to 50 °C
content: Employees at an ICA Kvantum supermarket in Sjoebo, Sweden, unload spoiled food from the freezer units. | Image: Johan Nilsson / TT News Agency / AFP via Getty Images Grocery stores across Europe have been hit by another wave of suspected cyberattacks, reporting sudden changes in the temperatures of their fridges and freezers. Major supermarket chains across Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg, and Estonia were affected, according to local reports shared by Bloomberg and Reuters. One Ica Kvantum store in Sweden said on its Facebook page that its fridges and freezers had been hacked overnight, with temperatures remotely raised to 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit). In a statement to Business Insider, a spokesperson at Swedish supermarket chain Coop also confirmed that "unauthorized actors were able to access and …
summary: Grocery stores in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg and Estonia experienced suspected cyberattacks that caused sudden temperature changes in their fridges and freezers. An ICA Kvantum store in Sjoebo, Sweden said its units were hacked overnight with temperatures raised to 50 °C, and Coop confirmed unauthorized actors accessed its systems.
author: The Verge

title: Affinity creative studio now free on iPad
content:
Canva has launched a free iPad version of Affinity’s creative studio. The new Affinity for iPad delivers the same pro‑grade tools that were offered in the desktop suite, covering vector graphics, photo editing, illustration and page layout, and it is optimized for Apple Pencil and touchscreens.

The iPad app also introduces a Sketch Studio feature aimed at freehand drawing and streamlining sketch‑to‑vector workflows, with tools for masking and automatically converting rough sketches into vector elements. The release follows Canva’s relaunch of the Affinity suite as an all‑in‑one desktop application last year.
summary: Canva has introduced Affinity for iPad, offering the same pro‑grade tools for vector graphics, photo editing, illustration and page layouts optimized for Apple Pencil and touchscreens. The iPad version adds a Sketch Studio for freehand drawing with masking tools and automatic conversion of rough sketches to vectors.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX in talks to acquire Boost Mobile to launch its own budget carrier
content:
SpaceX has reportedly explored a partnership with Boost Mobile to launch its own mobile service through the budget‑friendly carrier, according to a Washington Post report. The potential deal would see the Elon Musk‑owned company either acquire Boost Mobile or gain access to its network as part of an effort to make Starlink a “major” mobile carrier.

Musk discussed the possible agreement with Charlie Ergen, chairman of Boost Mobile’s parent company EchoStar, last month. Boost Mobile’s network is currently powered by T‑Mobile and AT&T, so SpaceX would likely need permission from those carriers to operate its service.
summary: SpaceX has discussed a deal with Boost Mobile to launch its own service through the budget-friendly carrier, according to a report from The Washington Post. The deal, which comes as SpaceX aims to make Starlink a "major" mobile carrier, reportedly involves the Elon Musk-owned company acquiring Boost Mobile or accessing its network.
author: The Verge

title: 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 price jumps to $385 after $80 increase
content:
The 16 GB model of the Raspberry Pi 5 is now priced at $385 after an $80 increase, raising its cost from the $120 launch price to more than three times that amount. The 16 GB versions of the Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 also saw a $40 rise, bringing their price range to $375‑$415.

Raspberry Pi CEO Eben Upton said the hikes are driven by a lack of “alternative supply” for 16 GB DRAM and broader component shortages. He described the increases as unavoidable and acknowledged they are unwelcome for customers.
summary: The Raspberry Pi 5 with 16GB of RAM now costs $385 after an $80 price hike, the latest in a string of increases driven by the ongoing RAM shortage. This configuration launched at $120 and now costs more than triple that price.
author: The Verge

title: Netflix signs Druski to exclusive deal; series Collect & Praise debuts Dec 1
content:
Netflix announced a multiyear agreement with YouTuber, comedian and influencer Druski to produce original content exclusively for the streaming platform. The deal follows Netflix’s recent strategy of signing creators such as Mark Rober, Ms. Rachel and Good Mythical Morning.

Druski’s first project under the partnership is “Collect & Praise,” a semi‑scripted comedy series in which he portrays a megachurch pastor. The series is slated to debut on December 1 and will be the initial installment of several original projects planned by Druski and his production company, 4LIFERS Entertainment.

A photo of Druski taken during MLB All‑Star Week on July 13, 2026, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, accompanies the announcement. The image is credited to Gilbert Carrasquillo / GC Images.
summary: Netflix announced a multiyear deal with YouTuber, comedian and influencer Druski to create original content exclusively for the streaming service. His first Netflix series, the semi‑scripted comedy Collect & Praise in which he plays a megachurch pastor, will debut on December 1 as the first of several projects from his company 4LIFERS Entertainment.
author: The Verge

title: Patti Zirhut says she will not vote for GOP gubernatorial nominee Byron Donalds
content:
Patti Zirhut, a lifelong Republican who supported Donald Trump in the 2016, 2020, and 2024 elections, says she is not following the party line this year. Zirhut describes her ballot as mixed, noting she plans to vote for some Republicans, independents, and Democrats. While she remains undecided in several races, she states with certainty that she will not vote for Byron Donalds, the Republican nominee for Florida governor.

Donalds holds President Trump’s endorsement and the support of the Republican Party. He also has access to $148 million in campaign funds. The article poses the question of whether backlash against data centers could influence the outcome of the Florida gubernatorial election.
summary: Patti Zirhut, a lifelong Republican who voted for Donald Trump in 2016, 2020 and 2024, is planning a mixed ballot with some Republicans, independents and Democrats. She says she will not vote for Byron Donalds, the Republican nominee for Florida governor who has Trump's endorsement and $148 million in campaign funds.
author: The Verge

title: $48 Seeed Studio TRMNL e‑paper kit lets users display any content
content:
A DIY e‑paper display kit priced at $48 is now available from Seeed Studio, a product developed in collaboration with TRMNL. According to the author, the kit allows users to show any content they choose and to operate with any software ecosystem they prefer.

The author previously created a similar device by modifying a Lenovo ThinkSmart View purchased on eBay for roughly $30 during a liquidation. Although the Lenovo hardware was originally designed for business‑to‑business video, it can run a fork of LineageOS, but its limited RAM results in sluggish performance.

Finding the TRMNL kit’s e‑paper display appealing, the author opted for the new Seeed Studio offering as a replacement for the earlier Lenovo‑based solution. The post concludes with a link to read the full article and a comments section.
summary: The author purchased a $48 DIY e‑paper display kit from Seeed Studio, developed with TRMNL, that can show whatever the user wants using any software ecosystem. Earlier they modded a Lenovo ThinkSmart View, which sold for about $30 on eBay but was sluggish because of limited RAM, leading them to choose the TRMNL kit.
author: Ars Technica

title: TechCrunch Founder Summit set for Nov. 4 in Boston with group discounts
content: The TechCrunch Founder Summit will take place on November 4 in Boston, offering a founder‑focused agenda and opportunities for impactful connections. Attendees can save up to $100 or receive discounts by purchasing group passes. The event’s promotion emphasizes that Boston founders do not need a Silicon Valley address to build something big.
summary: The TechCrunch Founder Summit will take place on November 4 in Boston and will feature a founder-focused agenda and opportunities for impactful connections. Attendees can save up to $100 or receive discounts by purchasing group passes.

title: Northwood Space raises $375M Series C at a $2B valuation from a16z and DFJ growth
content: Northwood Space, a space‑infrastructure company, announced on Monday that it closed a $375 million Series C financing round. The round was co‑led by Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth, and the investment values Northwood Space at $2 billion.
summary: Space infrastructure company Northwood Space on Monday said it had raised $375 million in a Series C round co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth, valuing the company at $2 billion.

title: Ninja launches first Crispi Microwave with FusionCrisp technology, replacing two appliances
content: Ninja has introduced its first microwave, the Ninja Crispi Microwave, which uses FusionCrisp technology to deliver microwave‑quick cooking while producing the crispy texture typical of an air fryer, allowing it to serve the functions of both appliances.
summary: Ninja introduced its first Crispi Microwave, which uses FusionCrisp technology to blend microwave speed with air‑fryer crispness. The reviewer says the appliance replaced two of their kitchen devices at once.
author: TechCrunch

title: Top 12 autumn must‑have products from garlic press to vitamin C serum
content:
Autumn’s cooler weather has prompted many to turn to indoor comforts, with casserole dishes, electric heaters and hot coffee featuring prominently in recent shopping choices. The shift in temperature has also encouraged people to “hunker down” and consider using radiators or portable electric heaters to stay warm.

At the same time, shoppers are looking ahead to the party season and reviving parts of their wardrobes that have been out of use since early spring. Items highlighted include a clothes steamer for refreshing garments, a pencil skirt, a sheer silk shirt and a vitamin C serum aimed at maintaining skin glow throughout the winter months. These products were identified as some of the favourite October purchases.
summary: The article lists twelve products that readers are currently favoring for the autumn season. Items mentioned include a garlic press, a vitamin C serum, a clothes steamer, a pencil skirt, a silk shirt, casserole dishes and electric heaters.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Naomi Klein and Ilana Glazer call for blocking reckless AI IPOs and taxing billionaires
content: We cannot let the billionaire class take unprecedented risks with our future America is a divided country in crisis. Despite the sunny economic forecast coming from the Trump administration, millions of Americans are struggling to find and keep jobs, getting crushed under the rising cost of living, and losing health insurance when they need it the most. Meanwhile, via corporate consolidation and political corruption, the billionaire class is getting richer faster than ever before: a 40% increase in wealth in just the last two years. Today, the combined wealth of nearly 3,000 global billionaires equals one-fifth of the entire world’s yearly output. Nearly 1,000 billionaires live and do business in the United States.
summary: Naomi Klein and Ilana Glazer call for blocking reckless AI IPOs and taxing billionaires.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Palantir AI platform claimed beneficial by 29 NHS trusts but many not using it
content: Exclusive: Gap between NHS claim and trusts’ comments described as ‘very misleading’ by senior health official More than two dozen hospital trusts the NHS claims have benefited from Palantir’s medical data platform are not using all or most of the AI-powered technology, the Guardian can reveal. The 29 hospital trusts that NHS England publicly lists as “realising benefits” from the controversial £330m federated data platform (FDP) have said the system is not live or they are not using any of its applications. The apparent gap between the NHS claim and the trusts’ understanding was described as “very misleading” by one senior health official.
summary: Palantir AI platform claimed beneficial by 29 NHS trusts but many not using it.

title: Prospect union to organise 7,000 Google UK workers after new union access rights
content: Trade unions are set to expand their presence in UK big‑tech firms after new employment‑rights legislation allowing union access to workplaces took effect. On Monday, Google UK signed an agreement with the Prospect union under which the union will hold workplace sessions and recruit members. The deal covers roughly 7,000 Google employees in the United Kingdom, including staff at YouTube, while workers at DeepMind are excluded from the arrangement.
summary: The Prospect union has reached an agreement with Google UK to organise about 7,000 workers across its UK operations, including YouTube but excluding DeepMind. The deal follows new UK employment rights that give unions workplace access, enabling further inroads into big‑tech firms.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Investors withdraw $3.6bn from Binance after $6.3bn hack linked to North Korea
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to permit withdrawals after a theft that experts believe originated in North Korea. The platform was hit on Thursday by a $6.3 billion theft, which has been described as the biggest heist in history. In response, investors have moved $3.6 billion (£2.7 billion) out of Binance as the exchange works to recover from the record hack. Experts have identified North Korea as the probable source of the theft.
summary: Investors withdraw $3.6bn from Binance after $6.3bn hack linked to North Korea.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Mbappé apologises after meme likening him to Mao, three Chinese firms end deals
content: Kylian Mbappé issued an apology after his remarks about a meme that portrayed him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong provoked backlash in China. The dispute led at least three Chinese companies to terminate brand agreements with the footballer, and it prompted a response from China’s Foreign Ministry.
summary: Kylian Mbappé apologized after remarks about a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong sparked backlash in China. At least three Chinese companies have ended brand deals with him, and the controversy prompted a response from China's Foreign Ministry.

title: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz in two days if US meets conditions
content: Iran announced it could reopen the Hormuz Strait within two days if the United States meets its conditions. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the revised timeline, shortened from a seven‑day proposal in September, reflects Iran’s good‑faith approach, but added that the outcome depends on Washington.
summary: Iran says it can reopen Hormuz within two days if the United States meets its conditions. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the timeline was shortened from a seven‑day proposal in September and that everything depends on Washington.
author: Euronews

title: Cyberattack disables refrigeration in Belgian supermarkets, fridges left empty
content: Supermarkets in Belgium and other European countries have reported cyberattacks that targeted refrigeration systems. The attacks caused food to spoil and forced some stores to shut down their fridges and freezers, leaving the refrigeration areas empty.
summary: Supermarkets in several European countries reported cyberattacks that targeted refrigeration systems. The attacks caused food to spoil and forced some stores to close off their fridges and freezers.

title: Italy has most journalists under police protection as threats increase
content: Italy has the highest number of journalists under police protection in Europe, reflecting a profession that faces frequent threats and intimidation. While the European Union has introduced measures intended to safeguard press freedom, the implementation of those protections is proceeding slowly.
summary: Italy has the largest number of journalists under police protection in Europe. Journalism in Italy is especially vulnerable to threats and intimidation, and EU measures to protect press freedom are being implemented slowly.

title: Fridge cyberattacks cause temperature spikes in supermarkets across five European countries
content: Stores and supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Finland, Estonia and Sweden reported abrupt temperature spikes in their fridges and freezers early Monday, which they attribute to an apparent cyberattack on refrigeration units. The incidents come after a comparable attack in October that affected hundreds of French supermarkets and resulted in food loss and fires.
summary: Stores and supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Finland, Estonia and Sweden reported abrupt temperature spikes in their fridges and freezers early Monday in an apparent cyberattack targeting refrigeration units. The incidents follow a similar attack that hit hundreds of supermarkets across France in October, triggering food loss and fires.

title: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El‑Sayed
content: France 24’s Fraser Jackson previewed the political landscape one day before the United States’ midterm elections, noting that both Democrats and Republicans were making their final appeals to voters. In Michigan, Democrat Haley Stevens drew attention by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers over the Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed. Stevens had previously lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to El‑Sayed in a contested race, and her cross‑party endorsement prompted accusations that she was acting out of “sour grapes.”
summary: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic candidate Abdul El‑Sayed in the state’s Senate race. She had lost the Michigan Democrats’ Senate primary to El‑Sayed, leading some to accuse her of sour grapes.

title: French high school protests resume Monday, targeting schools in Paris, Marseille, Rennes
content: French high‑school student protests resumed on Monday after a two‑week autumn break, but on a much smaller scale than in recent weeks. Pupils attempted to blockade a handful of high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes.
summary: French high school student protests resumed on Monday after a two‑week break. Pupils tried to blockade a few high schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes on a much smaller scale than in past weeks.

title: Argentina's President Milei eyes Patagonia as site for new data centres
content: Argentina’s President Javier Milei is advocating for an increase in data‑centre construction, and the government has identified the open steppes of Patagonia as a potentially suitable location. This follows broader global concerns about data‑centres’ noise, high power use and visual impact.
summary: Citizens and lawmakers worldwide are pushing back against data centre construction due to noise, power consumption and visual impact. President Javier Milei wants more data centres in Argentina and the government sees Patagonia's open steppes as a potential location.

content: Michigan’s Senate seat is described as a must‑win for the Democratic Party as it aims to gain control of the U.S. Senate. Progressive candidate Abdul El‑Sayed is reported to have a surge of energy behind him, particularly among younger voters, prompting questions about whether Gen Z enthusiasm will translate into votes and help Democrats secure the seat.

content: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia reported that cyberattacks compromised their emergency‑alert mobile applications. In Ukraine, users received false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat, while Moscow said hackers accessed the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s app to send fake alerts and are working to restore its functionality.
summary: Authorities in Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert mobile apps were targeted by cyberattacks, with Ukrainian users receiving false warnings of an imminent nuclear threat. Moscow said hackers accessed the Russian Emergency Situations Ministry’s app to send fake alerts and that work was underway to restore its functionality.

title: Richard Johnson says Trump’s unpopularity threatens Republicans in 2026 midterms
content: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections.

title: Nine dead as Learjet crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida
content:
A Learjet crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, Florida.  

The crash killed all nine people on board and left a large crater on the ground.
summary: A Learjet crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County. All nine people on board were killed and the impact left a large crater in the ground.

content: Ethiopia’s economy is currently expanding robustly. However, renewed fighting in the country’s northern region—a BRICS member—raises concerns that the conflict could deter investment, strain public finances and increase the cost of living.

content: Ryanair has announced that it is considering a pay freeze for its staff, a move that could lead to a confrontation with unions as the airline seeks to offset soaring fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict. content:
Supermarket chains across Europe have reported that the temperatures in refrigerators and freezers rose overnight, raising concerns of a second suspected cyber‑attack. The incident, affecting stores in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg, mirrors a previous hack that caused significant food losses in France.

content:

The court heard that Silvey had sent multiple messages expressing a sexual desire for young boys and had been caught in possession of explicit images of children and adults.

The ban, introduced nearly 11 months ago, requires ten platforms—Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads—to deactivate or suspend accounts of users they determine to be under 16 years old. The upcoming court case will be the first major legal test of the legislation.
summary: Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project, led by NSW state MP John Ruddick, are challenging Australia’s under‑16 social media ban in the High Court. title: MIT engineers develop water‑resistant microneedle vaccine system for farmed fish
content:
Fish raised in pools and ponds now supply a growing share of the world’s protein, but disease outbreaks can cause major losses for aquaculture producers.  Today’s most effective vaccination method for fish relies on metal needles, a process that requires sedating the fish, removing them from the water, and having workers inject each animal individually.  The technique is described as labor‑intensive, costly, stressful for fish, and risky for workers because of rapid handling, potential cross‑contamination and accidental needle sticks.

A team of researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the U.S. Department of Agriculture has introduced an alternative delivery platform that uses water‑resistant, food‑grade microneedles.  The microneedles are fabricated from silk fibroin and coated with a thin layer of shellac, an insect‑secreted resin commonly used in food coatings and pills.  This coating creates a moisture barrier that allows the microneedles to remain attached to fish skin, penetrate lightly, and then decompose after delivering their cargo.  The researchers reported that the system can store and release a range of vaccines, including bacterial vaccines and DNA plasmid vaccines, with release times that can be tuned from minutes to up to 24 hours.

The study, published in ACS Nano, demonstrated the technology on rainbow trout as small as one to two grams.  According to Gregory Wiens of the USDA National Center for Cool and Cold Water Aquaculture, the microneedles can pierce wet skin, stay attached while the fish swim, and release either bacterin or DNA vaccines in a controlled manner.  Laboratory tests showed that the microneedles preserved about half of the DNA plasmids’ structure after four weeks of dry storage, a feature the authors note could ease the need for cold‑chain logistics in rural aquaculture settings.

The work builds on prior silk microneedle research led by Benedetto Marelli, a professor in MIT’s Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering.  Marelli’s lab received support from the Abdul Latif Jameel Water and Food Systems Lab (J‑WAFS) and, beginning in 2022, biomedical engineer Meng Li joined the project.  Li, a postdoctoral researcher and first author of the paper, secured a USDA fellowship in 2024 that provided additional funding and connections, including access to a DNA vaccine for rainbow trout from the U.S. Geological Survey.

While the authors acknowledge that further development is needed before large‑scale farm deployment, they present the microneedle platform as a potentially safer and more efficient tool for vaccinating small fish, improving worker safety, and supporting the broader goal of expanding sustainable aquaculture production.  The research was funded in part by MIT’s J‑WAFS and the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
summary: Fish that are cultivated in pools or ponds are an increasingly important source of food around the world. Unfortunately, disease outbreaks can cause substantial losses in aquaculture.

content:

content:
Spanish authorities said a high‑speed train collision last week killed 69 people, making it one of Europe’s deadliest rail incidents of the century. Among the dead were 54 Spaniards, four U.S. citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic.

title: WA police facial recognition trial scans over 1.3 million faces, leads to 122 arrests
content:
Western Australian police completed a five‑month trial of real‑time facial‑recognition technology that scanned 1,380,882 faces. The system was deployed in 100 surveillance vans across 43 regional and metropolitan locations, concluding on Saturday.

The trial produced 122 arrests and led officers to engage with 146 registered sex offenders. It also generated nine false alerts, highlighting the technology’s potential for incorrect identifications.
summary: During a five‑month trial, Western Australia police used real‑time facial recognition in 100 deployments across 43 regional and metropolitan locations, scanning 1,380,882 faces. The trial, which ended on Saturday, led to 122 arrests and nine false alerts.

content:

The catch was part of a Northern Territory competition, and Maurice said, “I’m just happy to catch fish,” after landing the fish.

content:

title: Arsenal beat Liverpool to move three points clear at top of table
content: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team. Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them.
summary: Mikel Arteta secured his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, marking the champions' first league victory at Anfield in 14 years. The result moved Arsenal three points clear at the top of the table, while Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola had previously described the team's title bid as too early.

title: Sheila Chepkirui Wins Second NYC Marathon; Almgren Takes Men's Debut Title
content:
Sweden’s Andreas Almgren claimed the men’s title at the New York City Marathon on Sunday in his debut over the 26.2-mile distance. After a career focused on half marathons and the 10,000m, Almgren pulled away from Italy’s Yemaneberhan Crippa in the final mile to finish in two hours, six minutes, and one second. Crippa placed second, 13 seconds behind, while Lesotho’s Kamohelo Mofolo finished third, edging out defending champion Benson Kipruto.

In the women’s race, Kenya’s Sheila Chepkirui secured her second title. The United States’ Jessica McClain finished in second place.
summary: Sheila Chepkirui of Kenya won the women's race of the New York City Marathon for the second time. Sweden's Andreas Almgren claimed the men's title on his debut, finishing in 2:06:01 after pulling away from Yemaneberhan Crippa, who finished 13 seconds behind, with Kamohelo Mofolo of Lesotho taking third place over defending champion Benson Kipruto.

Liverpool were beaten by Kai Havertz’s early strike after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
content:
Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest driver to claim the Formula One world championship, securing the title with a third-place finish at the Mexican Grand Prix. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver clinched the crown with four races remaining in the season, marking his debut F1 title. By achieving this feat, Antonelli also became the first Italian to win the championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The race itself was won by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who finished ahead of Lewis Hamilton in second place. Hamilton’s teammate, Charles Leclerc, crossed the line in fourth position. The result represented a significant milestone for the Mercedes team, as it is their first drivers’ championship since Hamilton’s final victory in 2020 and the team’s 10th overall in the sport’s history.
summary: Kimi Antonelli, 20, clinched the Formula One world championship by finishing third in the Mexican Grand Prix, securing the title with four races remaining. He became the youngest driver to win the championship and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari, while Mercedes claimed its first drivers’ championship since Hamilton in 2020.

title: PolyU develops Tumour Heterogeneity Index to predict breast cancer AKT inhibitor response
content:
Researchers at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) have created an imaging biomarker called the Tumour Heterogeneity Index (THI). The THI allows a noninvasive assessment of breast cancer patients’ likely response to AKT inhibitors before treatment begins, enabling clinicians to identify those most likely to benefit.

In a study, patients with a high THI had an estimated pathological complete response (pCR) rate of 56.1%, markedly higher than patients with a low THI. The technology could help patients receive the most appropriate treatment earlier, reduce unnecessary side effects, and allow clinicians to better tailor treatment strategies to individual patients.

Golden State’s Golden State Valkyries captured their first WNBA title on Saturday night, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68‑63 in a Game 7 comeback that made them the fastest expansion team in major North American professional sports history to win a championship. The victory came just 534 days after the team’s inaugural game, a record that underscores the rapid rise of the franchise.

The championship roster included a point guard who had been dismissed by Dallas, a starting forward who had been waived five times, and a late‑blooming All‑Star who had been overlooked by every league team. These overlooked players found a coach who had built a career on making small openings count. Natalie Nakase, who earned a scholarship at UCLA from a walk‑on spot and secured a coaching position in Japan’s top men’s league after sending an unsolicited scouting report, brought a unique blend of trust and opportunity to the team.

Nakase’s circuitous journey taught her how to unlock potential in overlooked talent. The Valkyries’ success demonstrates the power of providing resources, responsibility, and trust to players who were once undervalued, proving the organization’s philosophy and Nakase’s leadership were key to their championship run.
summary: Natalie Nakase Leads Valkyries to WNBA Championship in 534 Days.

title: Premier League managers hold firm as first sacking looms after early season stability
content:
Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away.  No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season.  In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change, indicating that the early part of the campaign is often a period of stability.

The 2026‑27 season began with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026, a factor that has likely contributed to the current lack of dismissals.  The clubs have therefore been given a chance to shape their squads as they see fit without the pressure of an early change in leadership.

However, with roughly a quarter of the season already played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.  The looming break could prompt clubs to make a decision if results do not meet expectations.
summary: No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season, and all clubs began with the same manager. With roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.

title: Charisma as a Red Flag: How a Bar Conversation Revealed Manipulation
content: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired. We discussed topics I know little about: the instability of modern economies, the feasibility of commercial space travel, the likelihood of a coup in Russia. I found myself leaning in and asking questions: I felt as if I could learn a lot from this person. We eventually got to psychology, which is more my wheelhouse. I brooded about how easy it’s become for people to accept strange ideas. “Some people will believe anything,” he observed. “Some people even believe the Earth is round!” It’s increasingly difficult to ignore how fragmented and bizarre our beliefs have become. We live in our own echo chambers, defined by the channels, feeds and influencers we follow. As a result we can arrive at very polarised conclusions about vaccines, the climate, gender, geopolitics, the shape of the Earth and everything else. Disagreements on topics like these frequently damage relationships, alienate friends and estrange loved ones.
summary: The narrator recounts a conversation with a charismatic stranger in a bar who discussed topics the narrator knew little about, including economics, space travel, and geopolitics. The narrator reflects that charisma can lead people to accept bizarre ideas, contributing to polarized beliefs that damage relationships.

content:

Under the proposals, most migrants would have to wait about ten years, while some could face up to fifteen years before qualifying for settlement.

Indirect talks in Doha entered their third day on Sunday, with Qatar working to secure the release of more than $6 billion in Iranian assets. The effort is aimed at opening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

Officials from Gulf states say they are “braced for the worst” as they await Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait before the U.S. mid‑term elections on Tuesday. content:

The UK government has drawn up the framework for the fee parity, according to sources. It would enable EU students arriving from the continent to pay identical fees to those paid by domestic students.

The proposal is contingent on the UK gaining access to the European Union’s “Made in Europe” industrial programme, Brussels’ approval of which is a prerequisite for the fee‑equalisation plan.

content:

title: Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 Spacecraft Toward Mars on Nov. 1, 1962
content:
On November 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft, marking the country’s fourth attempt to send a probe to the Red Planet. The launch was part of the broader Space Race, and the mission’s objective was a fly‑by of Mars.

Immediately after separating from its launch vehicle, Mars 1 deployed its solar panels and entered a cruise phase toward Mars. Mission controllers received telemetry that revealed a leak in one of the gas valves that controlled the spacecraft’s orientation system. With the orientation system compromised, the probe could not reliably point its antennas toward Earth, and contact was lost when the spacecraft was roughly halfway to Mars.

Despite the loss of communication, Mars 1 did reach Mars and performed a fly‑by, providing the first close‑approach data about the planet. The mission was the Soviet Union’s first to get near enough to reveal early details about Mars, although it was not considered a complete success due to the orientation failure and loss of contact.

Mars 1’s launch followed three earlier Soviet attempts that ended in launch failures. Two years later, NASA’s Mariner IV became the first successful fly‑by mission to Mars. The 1962 Soviet mission remains a notable milestone in early interplanetary exploration.

For additional space‑history content, the “On This Day In Space” archive and related videos are available on YouTube.
summary: The Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on Nov. 1, 1962, to fly by Mars. It lost contact with Earth about halfway to the planet after a gas valve leak caused a loss of orientation.

title: Young Vic to livestream Milo Rau’s documentary play on Gisèle Pelicot trial on Nov 30
content:
The Young Vic’s upcoming production of Milo Rau’s four‑hour documentary play about the trial of the men who drugged and raped Gisèle Pelicot is set to run at London’s County Hall on 30 November. The show, created with Servane Dècle, has already been performed worldwide and sold out quickly. It will be livestreamed in full, offering audiences a chance to experience the piece from home.

Rau, a Swiss director known for his “ripped‑from‑the‑headlines” approach, has previously staged works on wars in Iraq and Congo and on the exploitation of migrant workers. His new play focuses on the factual details of the trial rather than conventional theatrical set pieces, a point highlighted by Young Vic boss Nadia Fall.

The cast features Adjoa Andoh, Rosie Jones and Olivia Williams. Fall remarked that the act of witnessing the facts “really got me” and that the production “just floors you.”
summary: The four‑hour documentary play about the trial of the men who drugged and raped Gisèle Pelicot, created by Milo Rau with Servane Dècle, will be staged by the Young Vic at London’s County Hall on 30 November. The sold‑out production, starring Adjoa Andoh, Rosie Jones and Olivia Williams, will be livestreamed in full.

title: Ariarne Titmus discusses retirement, health, and intense former coach
content: The Australian swimming great on her decision to retire, her health and fertility journey – and her ‘intense’ former coach From a life tracing the black line three metres below the water’s surface, to one marked by shades of grey, Ariarne Titmus is still adapting. Now 26, and two years removed from her final competitive event, she recognises her excellence as a swimmer only partly prepared her for what came next. “I look at a lot of things in my life pretty black and white, which is probably not a good way to be sometimes,” she says. “In my swimming career, I was all or nothing. I was win or lose. I was achieve it, or fail. And I guess that’s not a great way to be in life.”
summary: Australian swimmer Ariarne Titmus reflects on her retirement, health, and fertility journey. She acknowledges that her previous all-or-nothing competitive mindset was not ideal for life outside of swimming.

title: Harriet Dart wins maiden WTA title at 30 in Guangzhou Open
content:
Britain’s Harriet Dart claimed her maiden WTA title at the Guangzhou Open in China by defeating 18-year-old Austrian Lilli Tagger with a score of 4-6, 6-3, 6-4. The 30-year-old qualifier, ranked as the British No 5, came from a set down to secure the victory in what was her first WTA final.

Dart’s path to the final included a semi-final win over Sun Xinran, during which she saved three match points. In the final match against the fourth seed, Dart dropped her serve in the opening game and faced a break point in her subsequent service game before establishing a foothold. Although she broke back to reach 4-4, Tagger, who won the 2025 junior French Open, responded to take the first set.
summary: Briton Harriet Dart, 30, won her first WTA title at the Guangzhou Open after defeating 18‑year‑old Lilli Tagger 4‑6, 6‑3, 6‑4. The qualifier saved three match points in her semi‑final win over Sun Xinran and is ranked British No 5.

content:

The loss has left United in 17th place in the Premier League, marking their first win in nine games and their poorest start to a season since 1988.

No managerial change is anticipated until the international break. Carrick’s position is set to be reviewed again after the next round of Premier League fixtures, during which United will host Aston Villa next Sunday.

title: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34
content:
Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34, her family announced. The athlete, who is from Portaferry in Northern Ireland, passed away at 6.30am on Sunday. Mageean was a two-time Olympic competitor who secured the European 1500m title in Rome in 2024.

In a social media post, her family stated that she was surrounded by her loved ones at the time of her death. They described her as a “beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many,” noting that she will be deeply missed.
summary: Ciara Mageean, European 1500m gold medallist with Ireland, dies aged 34.

content:

content:

content: New research from The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center has identified a previously unknown mechanism that enables cancer cells to selectively produce tumor‑driving proteins such as KRAS in common cancers. title: Clot removal after stroke may aid recovery but carries risks
content:
After a stroke, doctors treat time as a critical factor. Each minute that blood cannot reach the brain raises the risk of permanent damage or death.  

Endovascular thrombectomy offers a way to restore circulation. The minimally invasive procedure physically removes the clot, reestablishes blood flow, and can markedly lower the risk of long‑term disability or death.  

Because of its effectiveness, mechanical thrombectomy is the standard emergency treatment for acute ischemic stroke within the first 24 hours after the event.
summary: After a stroke, each minute of blocked blood flow increases the risk of permanent brain damage. Endovascular thrombectomy, a minimally invasive clot‑removal procedure, can restore circulation and lower the chance of long‑term disability or death and is a standard emergency treatment within the first 24 hours of an acute ischemic stroke.

title: Trump administration proposes cash for married parents to stay home, experts question adequacy
content:
The Trump administration has proposed a program that would provide financial assistance to married parents who choose to stay at home. Experts say the plan emphasizes “traditional families” and does not account for the broader flexibility many households need to support themselves.

Erica Hall’s experience illustrates those concerns. She and her husband spaced their children five years apart to avoid the cost of two daycare spots, self‑funded her first maternity leave with savings, and was recently laid off from her tech job, leaving her uncertain about how to manage childcare expenses.
summary: The Trump administration has proposed a program that would give married parents money to stay at home. Experts say the proposal favors traditional families and may not provide enough flexibility for all families, as illustrated by Erica Hall’s experience with costly childcare and a recent job loss.

title: Affordability dominates voter concerns ahead of Tuesday midterms as Ohio strike nears record
content:

The cost‑of‑living pressure has dominated this election cycle, prompting workers and unions to back candidates who promise higher wages and measures to curb rising prices.

In Lorain County, Ohio, the issue is reflected locally: Gina Jones and her co‑workers at Lorain County Job and Family Services have been on strike since February 2026. The walkout is the longest public‑sector strike in Ohio’s history and could become the longest on record in the United States.

content: An interdisciplinary team at Marburg University applied modern natural‑product analysis together with Egyptology and the history of pharmacy to a 2,700‑year‑old mummy head. Their study produced the first molecular evidence that aloe was used in ancient Egyptian embalming.
summary: Researchers identified molecular traces of aloe in a 2,700‑year‑old mummy head, linking the plant to ancient Egyptian embalming. The interdisciplinary team at Marburg University used modern natural product analysis combined with Egyptology and pharmacy history to make the discovery.

content: Adopting permanent daylight‑saving time in British Columbia, the Northwest Territories, Alberta, Manitoba and northwestern Ontario would end the semi‑annual clock changes.
